title: Runbook for investigating SLI degradations in analytics ingestion
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose:
This ticket delivers a pragmatic, step-by-step investigation playbook (runbook) for SLI degradations observed in the Console analytics ingestion pipeline. The goal is to reduce time-to-identify root cause for tenant-impacting or global SLI regressions, standardize alert routing, and provide run-time diagnostic checklists and query snippets for on-call and SRE rotations.

Scope:
- SLIs covered: ingestion_latency_p50/p95, ingestion_error_rate, event_drop_ratio, downstream-join-failure_rate.
- Observability signals: traces (distributed spans across ingest -> transform -> store), structured logs (tenant_id, batch_id, sequence_id), metrics (per-route latency, queue_depth, backpressure signals), and dashboard views.
- Target components: analytics-ingest-service, transform-worker, dedupe/aggregation layer, metrics-ingest-proxy.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use a two-tier alert strategy: fast, noisy p50-based alerts for triage and p95/p99 for escalation. This reduces pager fatigue while keeping sensitivity for high-severity regressions.
- Preserve high-cardinality tenant IDs only in traces and short-term logs (14-day retention) and use hashed tenant token in metrics to keep cardinality manageable. Security and compliance were consulted: see Confluence note.
- Lightweight sampling for traces during high-volume incidents (adaptive sampling guided by ENG-34567 recommendations) to reduce storage cost but keep causal traces for top offenders.

Runbook (high-level):
1) Triage entry: Confirm alert and scope by checking alert tags (route, tenant_hash, cluster). Pull linked incident dashboard.
2) Quick health checks (5 minutes): check queue_depth, downstream_write_rate, and any autoscaling events.
3) Trace-first debugging: find a representative request id or batch_id; follow trace from ingress to storage to identify slow spans or retries. Use the provided trace query snippet in Confluence.
4) Log correlation: cross-reference span IDs with structured logs (log query snippets included). Look for repeated errors, retries, or backpressure headers.
5) Metrics validation: inspect aggregation windows for p50/p95 divergence, check for sudden cardinality shifts that indicate a new tenant or integration spike.
6) Isolation: if tenant-scoped, apply temporary per-tenant slowdown or route to degraded path (see routing playbook).
7) Mitigation + rollback: if a config or deploy caused regression, follow the Deploy Rollback checklist and notify stakeholders.
8) Post-incident: create an RCA ticket and adjust SLO targets or alerts if needed.

Dashboards and queries included:
- Tenant-level ingestion SLI dashboard (URL: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/analytics-sli-dashboard)
- Trace query templates for Jaeger/OpenTelemetry (examples in linked doc)
- Log search snippets with recommended fields (tenant_id, batch_id, span_id, error_code)

Acceptance criteria:
- Runbook document live in Confluence with verified query snippets.
- Two new dashboard widgets (p50 vs p95 delta and per-tenant error-rate heatmap) deployed to production console dashboards.
- Alert routing configured: initial triage to Analytics on-call, escalation to SRE if p95 exceeds threshold for 10m.
- Playbook verified in tabletop drill with on-call team.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/analytics-sli-runbook-draft
- PR for dashboard widgets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-dashboard/pull/4212
- Trace sampling RFC referenced: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/021-trace-sampling.md

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add automated tenant-exclusion heuristics to prevent noisy tenants from polluting global SLI? (Action: discuss with PM)
- Determine retention adjustments for high-volume trace snippets (cost vs signal trade-off).

Outcome expectations:
- Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) for SLI degradations in analytics from ~42 minutes to <15 minutes for the on-call rotation.
- Clear escalation paths and reproducible diagnostics to speed mitigation and RCA creation.
